name: gene-hooks
description: Hooks for every Claude Code session of Gene's: a bootstrap loader (hooks/boot.sh) that runs each hook from the newest installed version, the Pacific clock on every prompt and tool result (on a Skill call's result, since 1.20.0, SMADPickleBot #1169, a pointer to the newest installed copy of the skill when the session loaded an older one, so a long-running session never follows a stale skill; and on the clock's prompt branch, since 1.16.0, the model check, SMADPickleBot #423: once an hour per box, builtins only, the prompted desktop session is told to read the weekly Fable window with get_usage and set every desktop session to the newest Opus at 99% or back to the newest Fable after the reset, its own by a peer, a session on another machine by message (1.18.0), and since 1.17.0 to start the account handover once at 99% of the all-models window; since 1.19.0, SMADPickleBot #1144, once every session is on Opus the check holds until the Fable window's weekly reset, recorded by hooks/model-check-hold.sh, reading only the all-models window meanwhile; CLAUDE_MODEL_CHECK_OFF=1 turns it off), the Stop hook that makes every final reply open and close with its stamp and the ticket it works on (`· ticket: #N` or `ticket: none`, since 1.13.0) and rest any claim of who built a file, or how production stands, on something read that turn (since 1.15.0 a held reply is answered by one short line, never sent again), the PreToolUse gate that refuses a tool call whose preceding line has no stamp, a stamp naming no ticket, or one ahead of the clock (a final reply's stamp must be within a minute of it) or a task list left on one step for 12 tool calls (and, since 1.14.0, appends each passing call's `<epoch> <session> <tickets>` to the local activity log TICKET_ACTIVITY_LOG, ~/.claude/ticket-activity.log, with the Stop hook's `stop` line, so a project can count working time per ticket off the prompt; since 1.21.0, SMADPickleBot #1164, a call of Agent or Workflow writes `<epoch> <session> <tickets> delegated <tool_use_id>` and a subagent's own calls `<epoch> <session> agent <agent_id> <tool_use_id|->`, the parent call's id read from the agent's meta file when the Agent tool spawned it and `-` for a Workflow's agents, whose meta has none, so a ticket built by delegates counts their time too), the guard that refuses a long runner in the foreground and a PowerShell call that would strip the double quotes inside a native program's argument, and session-start checks for unpushed commits (its 10-minute rescan a detached job since 1.12.0, so a prompt pays stats and reads only), a stale install and (on Gene's Windows box) launches that would pop up a console window; and since 1.22.0 the session nanny (hooks/nanny.py, SMADPickleBot #1214), on PostToolUse and Stop: a background Bash run recorded from its start's result, and one that prints a wait, prints nothing for its first 30 s or stops growing for 120 s put in front of the session once at its next tool result, holding the turn's Stop once while it runs unexplained (NANNY_QUIET names commands quiet by design).
